intro: Trang is a city you can explore at a comfortable pace. The old town around the Clock Tower, a natural lake in the middle of the city that puts on a dancing-fountain show in the evenings, and a century-old wooden railway station in Kantang. Here are the 10 attractions people visiting Trang actually go to.

blocks.html:
Trang is a small city that's more rewarding to walk around than people expect. In the Thap Thiang district at the heart of town, Trang Clock Tower stands in classic style at a roundabout intersection — the city's landmark meeting point. Around it runs an old commercial district and local restaurants you can wander all day. A little further is Sra Kapang Surinthon Park, a shady natural pond in the middle of the city where locals come to run and cycle, and in the evening a Dugong Circle fountain with a dugong statue — the provincial symbol — makes for a favourite photo stop. For night activity, Cinta Garden Night Market is the garden-style evening market, or on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays the walking street in front of Trang Railway Station fills up with street food.

What people often mention about Trang is that the standout attractions hold up on inspection. Kantang Railway Station is a single-storey hip-roof wooden building in mustard yellow and brown that has been running since 1913 — the southern terminus of the Andaman line and a registered ancient monument. The vintage photo angles are excellent. For nature, Southern Botanical Garden (Thung Khai) has Thailand's first canopy walkway — 175 metres long, up to 18 metres high — where you walk through the tree canopy and might spot squirrels, birds, and monkeys. It's free. The combination of landmarks, evening markets, a city park, and a forest nature trail makes Trang the kind of place where a single trip genuinely covers multiple styles of travel.

blocks.name: Koh Kradan
blocks.signature: A white-sand island in the Andaman Sea voted world's best beach 2023 — and Thailand's only underwater wedding ceremony site
blocks.priceRange: National park entry: Thais 40 THB adults, foreigners 200 THB (boat not included)
blocks.descHtml:
Koh Kradan is a small island in the Andaman Sea in Kantang District, Trang, largely under the care of Hat Chao Mai National Park. It's the most talked-about island in Trang's sea zone: in 2023 the UK's World Beach Guide voted it the most beautiful beach in the world. The island's appeal is powder-white sand, water so clear you can see the seabed, and a quiet, uncommercialized pace — almost no traffic, no cluttered shopfronts. A proper place to sit and listen to waves.

What makes Koh Kradan stand out beyond the beach is the underwater wedding ceremony, held every year around 13–15 February, with the actual ceremony on Valentine's Day. Couples in wetsuits sign the marriage registry underwater among coral — a Guinness World Record for most participants at an underwater wedding. The ceremony is open to couples of any gender, making Koh Kradan a genuinely romantic island by reputation.

Around the island there's shallow-water snorkelling from the beach — staghorn coral, brain coral, schools of fish in several colours. The view from the beach stretches to Koh Muk, Koh Chueak, and Koh Ngai in the distance. You can only reach the island by boat, mostly from Pak Meng pier or Khuan Tungku pier, around 40 minutes to 1.5 hours depending on boat type. National park entry: Thais 40 THB for adults, foreigners 200 THB. Best season is November through April when seas are calm and boats run frequently.

A few practical notes: the island has almost no convenience shops and phone signal comes and goes. Bring cash, drinking water, and essentials from the mainland. For the clearest water and best photos, arrive in the morning before tour-boat crowds build up — you'll get the island at its quietest and most beautiful.
mustOrder: Shallow snorkelling on the coral reef from the beach
Swimming in clear water on white sand
Sunset view from the island shore
blocks.bestFor: Beach lovers who want clear water, white sand, and a calm atmosphere
blocks.hours: Open daily during daylight hours (boat schedule); closed during monsoon approximately mid-May–mid-Oct
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Koh Kradan, Trang · Tournasol7 · Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

blocks.name: Emerald Cave, Koh Muk
blocks.signature: Swim 80 metres through a pitch-dark tunnel to emerge in a hidden lagoon at the centre of the island — emerald-green water walled by sheer limestone cliffs
blocks.descHtml:
Emerald Cave is on the west side of Koh Muk, Kantang District, Trang, within Hat Chao Mai National Park — one of the most famous sea caves in the Andaman region. What draws people from around the world is the entrance: a small opening in a cliff face, through which you swim in complete darkness for about 80 metres before suddenly breaking out into a hidden beach inside the island, surrounded by sheer limestone walls rising like a giant shaft open to the sky. When sunlight hits the water inside, it turns a deep emerald green — hence the name.

The experience people talk about most is not just the hidden beach but the swim through the tunnel. Midway in, it's dark enough that you can't see your own hand. You hold a rope or follow a guide until you see light at the other end and emerge into the lagoon. Many people describe it as a genuinely spine-tingling moment. The emerald colour is at its most vivid from around 10:00 to 14:00 when sunlight angles directly in and reflects off the cave walls. Coming too early or too late will still show you the cave and the beach, but the water won't have that intensity of colour.

The main route in is by longtail or tour boat from Pak Meng or Khuan Tungku pier, or as part of a Trang island-hopping tour that usually includes the Emerald Cave in its itinerary. The cave itself has no entry fee, though national park fees may apply in the area. Tours provide life jackets and a guide to swim through. Open season is roughly November–April when the Andaman is calm. During the monsoon, rough water and strong currents sometimes close the cave — always check with your boat operator or the national park before booking.

Advice from people who've done it: aim for mid-tide, not dead high or dead low. At very high tide the tunnel ceiling is low and the swim is awkward; at very low tide the inner beach dries out and you won't see the green water. Getting there in the morning before the large tour boats arrive gives you the hidden beach quiet and uncrowded. Even weak swimmers can manage with a life jacket and guide, but anyone with claustrophobia should prepare mentally before entering the tunnel.
mustOrder: Swim the 80-metre dark tunnel
Hidden beach and lagoon at the centre of the island
Emerald water at its best mid-morning to early afternoon
blocks.bestFor: Adventurous visitors who want to swim into a hidden lagoon
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Emerald Cave, Koh Muk, Trang · Nik Cyclist · Wikimedia Commons · CC BY 2.0

blocks.name: Trang Clock Tower
blocks.area: City centre, Mueang District (in front of the Provincial Hall, near Trang Railway Station, Thap Thiang Sub-district)
blocks.signature: Classic clock tower at a roundabout — the city's meeting point and a well-known photo spot, surrounded by an old commercial district and local restaurants
blocks.descHtml:
If you're visiting Trang for the first time, the Clock Tower is the natural first stop — it stands prominently at the main four-way roundabout in front of the Provincial Hall, just a few minutes' walk from Trang Railway Station. It's the city's meeting point and the hub from which you fan out to all the different districts. The tower itself has a classic build, roughly 15 metres tall. The old locals called it "Ho Laeng Dai" — the Talking Tower — when it was a wooden municipal broadcasting tower, before it became the landmark clock tower it is today. Ideal for those who collect city landmarks, fans of old-town walking, and families who want a proper city photo.

The unmissable highlight is the photo angle with the tower itself, especially in the evenings after it is lit up. Since the recent renovation in vintage yellow tones, the tower looks crisp and photographs very well. Several reviews say the closer you walk, the more clearly you see the old architectural details. Around it is the original commercial district with shophouses in Sino-Portuguese style — a quiet, easy old-town atmosphere where you can wander and shoot photos at leisure.

There's also the food angle: around the clock tower there are plenty of local shops to stop at. Reviews mention a yen ta fo stall right next to the tower where people sit eating while looking up at it — so one stop covers both the photo and the meal. Free to enter — it's a public space open 24 hours. No entry fee. Come any time, but the evening is recommended for comfortable temperature and good light when the tower is illuminated. Located on Wiset Kul Road, Thap Thiang Sub-district, near the dolphin fountain roundabout.

The Clock Tower is popular because it genuinely is the heart of the city. During festivals it becomes a congregation point — New Year countdown with fireworks and a stage, and Songkran water-play that's lively every year. One practical note: it's an active roundabout with moving traffic. When crossing to the central island to take photos, watch for vehicles carefully, especially if you have children.
mustOrder: Classic clock-tower photo at the roundabout — lit up in vintage yellow in the evening
Walk the old commercial district and Sino-Portuguese shophouses around it
Stop at a local food stall near the clock tower
Festival atmosphere — New Year countdown and Songkran gatherings
blocks.bestFor: Quick landmark photo and a starting point before exploring the old town — evening into night
blocks.hours: Open 24 hours daily (best in the evening when the lights come on)

blocks.name: Kantang Railway Station
blocks.signature: A single-storey mustard-yellow hip-roof wooden building over 100 years old — southern terminus of the Andaman line, registered ancient monument, excellent vintage photo angles, with local products sold inside
blocks.descHtml:
If you like old places that are still alive, Kantang Railway Station is the stop you cannot skip. It's the final station of the southern railway line on the Andaman side, open since 1913. The building is a single-storey hip-roof wooden structure in mustard yellow and brown — the kind you recognize immediately as a classic Thai railway station from the old days. The Fine Arts Department has registered it as an ancient monument. Perfect for vintage photo fans, history enthusiasts, and families who want to show children a real old train.

The unmissable highlight is the wooden building itself, which still has all its original carved fretwork details intact. The front of the station with its name sign is the most popular photo point. Behind the station a vintage railway carriage sits on display and you can walk right up to it. Inside the station, local products are sold — shrimp paste, dried shrimp, Trang souvenirs. Reviews often praise how clean and quiet it is, with staff who enjoy telling old stories. Anyone who wants to extend the visit will find a café called Love Station next door — air-conditioned, good for a coffee sit-down.

Very easy on the budget: walking around and photographing the station is completely free. For the full atmosphere, time your visit for when the train arrives — there's only one service per day (express train 167/168, Bangkok–Kantang), arriving in the late morning and departing in the afternoon. The station is in the town of Kantang on Na Khai Road, about 40 minutes by car from Trang city. Plenty of cafés and food shops around to extend your visit.

The station is popular because it's simultaneously a vintage photo landmark and a rare southern terminal on the Andaman side. Practical note: train services are infrequent — if you plan to actually ride the train, check the State Railway of Thailand schedule in advance. But if you're just stopping to photograph and absorb the old atmosphere, any time of day delivers.
mustOrder: Mustard-yellow hip-roof wooden building — the vintage photo point
Vintage railway carriage on display behind the station
Local products: shrimp paste, dried shrimp, Trang souvenirs
Love Station café next door
blocks.bestFor: Vintage photo lovers and railway history fans
blocks.hours: Open daily during daytime and evening (one train service per day)

blocks.name: Sra Kapang Surinthon Park
blocks.area: Mueang Nakhon Trang Municipality, Mueang District, Trang
blocks.signature: A large natural pond of about 74 rai with a central pavilion connected by bridges, shady old trees, a running and cycling track around the lake, and an evening dancing-fountain and water-curtain show that has become a new photo spot
blocks.descHtml:
Sra Kapang Surinthon is Trang's oldest public park — a large natural pond of about 74 rai (roughly 30 acres; about 52 rai of water and 22 rai of land) right in the centre of the Mueang Nakhon municipality, about 2 kilometres from the Provincial Hall. An easy reach. Good for anyone who wants a shady place to sit near the city, for exercise lovers, and for families who want to bring children to feed the fish. The point most people mention is the central pavilion connected by bridges — walk out to the middle of the lake and feel the cool breeze. It's been a classic Trang photo spot for years.

The new highlight that has brought the park back to life is the dancing fountain and water-curtain show that has become a favourite evening check-in spot. The dancing fountain runs every day — evenings around 19:30–20:30 (with daytime rounds in the morning and afternoon as well). The illuminated water-curtain display is especially striking on Saturday and Sunday evenings. Reviews from regular visitors say coming in the evening gives a better atmosphere than the relatively hot midday. Around the lake there's a flat running and cycling track, shaded by large trees, with open lawns, outdoor exercise equipment, and rest pavilions at intervals.

Free entry, no fee. Open every day approximately 06:00–21:00. Best times are early morning for those running, or late afternoon into evening for the fountain show and photos. Visitors note that midday sun is fairly strong and in-park parking is limited. If you're coming for the evening show on a holiday, allow extra time to find parking. Some older structures in the park show their age, but overall it remains a valued green lung in the city centre that locals are attached to and visitors can stroll for an hour or two.
mustOrder: Dancing fountain and water-curtain show in the evening
Central pavilion connected by bridges over the lake
Running/cycling track around the lake
Feed the fish in the natural pond
blocks.bestFor: Morning or evening walk/exercise and watching the fountain show after dark
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative photo: Street food · Charles Haynes / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 2.0)

blocks.name: Southern Botanical Garden (Thung Khai) — Canopy Walkway
blocks.signature: Over 2,600 rai of tropical rainforest — the highlight is Thailand's first nature-study canopy walkway, 175 metres long, at 3 levels between 10 and 18 metres high, where you walk through the tree canopy and watch birds, squirrels, and monkeys. Free entry.
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Trang and want to escape the heat into a real forest without driving far, Southern Botanical Garden (Thung Khai) is the answer. It's a tropical rainforest of over 2,600 rai (about 1,040 acres) in the Thung Khai Forest Reserve, Yan Ta Khao District, only about 11–13 kilometres from the city. Suitable for families with children exploring nature, light-trail walkers, and anyone who wants a proper lungful of forest air without climbing a mountain. The centrepiece everyone talks about is Thailand's first canopy walkway — 175 metres long, rising 10–18 metres from the ground, linking six towers. You walk up through the levels from the forest floor all the way to the canopy top.

What makes this place special is that it's genuinely wild forest, not a manicured garden. Reviews consistently describe it as feeling like actual deep jungle — quiet, shaded, the kind of place where you look down through layers of canopy. If you're lucky you'll spot squirrels, birds, butterflies, lizards; sometimes monkeys appear. The aerial view from the towers makes for excellent photos, which is why the walkway has become one of Trang's most praised check-in spots. A complete loop of the trail is about 3 kilometres and takes roughly 1.5–3 hours depending on how long you pause for photos.

The budget case is strong: free entry, large parking area, open daily approximately 08:00–16:00 (some days closing at 16:30). Best time to come is morning to early afternoon when the air is cool and the light is good. Reviews note that some sections of the metal walkway have started to rust and creak, and the peat-forest trail sections can be slippery after rain — wear shoes with good grip. Some signs are in Thai only. Anyone with a fear of heights should prepare for the upper towers. But overall the experience of walking through forest from an unusual angle is well worth it, and it's not surprising that Thung Khai regularly appears at the top of Trang's most-praised attraction lists.
mustOrder: Canopy walkway — 175 m long, 10–18 m high
Climb the towers and see tree canopy at three levels
Walk the tropical rainforest nature trail, ~3 km
Spot squirrels, birds, and butterflies in the forest
blocks.bestFor: Families and nature walkers — come in the morning to early afternoon

blocks.name: Dugong Circle
blocks.area: Thap Thiang Sub-district, Mueang Trang District
blocks.signature: A fountain roundabout featuring a dugong sculpture — the provincial symbol of Trang — with other sea-creature statues, and coloured illumination in the evenings
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Trang for the first time and want a clear photo proving you've arrived, the Dugong Circle is where most people stop first. It's a fountain roundabout in the middle of the city with a prominent dugong sculpture at the centre — the dugong being the provincial symbol of Trang. Around it are other sea-creature sculptures and decorative details. A good stop for landmark photo collectors, families with children, and anyone driving through who wants a quick pause.

The highlight is the multi-tiered fountain with the white dugong as the centrepiece — several reviews compare its elegance to a palace fountain. The key is to come in the evening when the colour-changing lights come on, making the fountain significantly more photogenic than during the day. If you're visiting in a group, group shots work well here, and you can continue on foot to the nearby Governor's Residence or Thap Thiang Park.

No cost whatsoever — it's a public roundabout, free to walk around and photograph. Most people spend under an hour. The roundabout is on Phatthalung Road, Thap Thiang Sub-district, Mueang Trang District, near the approach to the Governor's Residence, close to the evening market and the government district. Easy to stop in on the way to other city attractions. Open all hours — it's a traffic roundabout, so accessible around the clock.

It's popular because it's the city's easiest check-in spot — central, accessible, and clearly expresses Trang's identity through the dugong. Google rating 4.3 from over 430 reviewers. Important practical note: it is a live traffic roundabout. Reviews often warn about vehicles and motorcycles when crossing to photograph — look both ways carefully, especially with children. Avoid midday when the sun is intense.
mustOrder: Dugong sculpture at the fountain roundabout
Colour-changing lights in the evening
Sea-creature statues around the circle
Continue to the nearby Governor's Residence or Thap Thiang Park
blocks.bestFor: First visit to Trang — quick landmark stop, great in the evening with the lights on
blocks.hours: Open 24 hours (recommended evening–night for the light display)

blocks.name: Cinta Garden Night Market
blocks.signature: Garden-style night market open around 17:00–23:00 daily — street food, chill-out spots, live music, and multiple photo zones including a red-brick wall, a Korean-Japanese-style café, and pretty night-lighting
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Trang for the evening and want one place that covers eating, hanging out, and photos in a single visit, Cinta Garden Night Market — sometimes called just Cinta or Cinta City — is the first name locals will give you. It's a garden-style night market in the city centre, spread across several rai, arranged in zones of one- and two-storey container buildings, a long stretch of street-food stalls in multiple rows, and a section for clothing, bags, and accessories. Works well whether you've come as a couple, with friends, or with family for an evening stroll after dinner.

The highlights people talk about most are the photo zones — a vintage-style red-brick wall, cute Korean- and Japanese-themed café corners, and attractive night lighting that photographs well. On the food side, dishes mentioned frequently in reviews include grilled pork neck, takoyaki, jok with a hundred toppings, and a corn and fermented fish dip with cockles — punchy flavours with real seasoning. Follow with desserts and cold drinks. On some evenings there's live music, a chill-out communal area, and a spot to watch football for sports fans.

Free entry. Street food mostly starts at a few tens of baht; sit down for a full evening and you'll spend around 150–300 THB per person. Food options span halal to vegetarian, so it's accessible for a mix of Thai and international visitors. Location in the Thap Thiang area of Mueang Trang District, a 15-minute walk from the Clock Tower. Open daily approximately 17:00–23:00.

What makes Cinta popular is that it's a well-organized night market with proper seating and a garden atmosphere that's hard to find at a regular outdoor market. Multiple real reviews describe it as the best-looking night market of Trang's options. A small practical note: parking is still not fully organized — on holidays it gets crowded, so arriving a little earlier makes finding a spot and a seat much easier.
mustOrder: Grilled pork neck
Takoyaki
Jok with a hundred toppings
Corn and fermented fish dip with cockles
blocks.bestFor: Evening dinner and a stroll — good for couples or groups

blocks.name: Trang Andaman Gateway
blocks.area: Chong Sub-district, Na Yong District, Trang
blocks.signature: Gateway to the Andaman on Khao Phap Pha — a 25-rai site with life-size elephant sculptures (the symbol of Trang tourism), plus sea-creature statues and a Tuk Tuk with a frog head; a roadside rest stop with mountain views before entering the city
blocks.descHtml:
Trang Andaman Gateway — locals call it "The Gateway to the Andaman" — is a rest stop on Khao Phap Pha, Highway 4 at the Trang–Phatthalung provincial border, before entering Trang city. If you're driving in from Phatthalung or Hat Yai, this is the first point that welcomes you to the Andaman side. On a site of about 25 rai, the highlight that makes every visitor stop and get out for a photo is the life-size elephant sculpture herd. Elephants were chosen as the symbol because more than a hundred years ago, when the road across the Banthat mountain range was being cut, elephants actually hauled timber and stone to build it. Ideal for road-trip drivers who want to stretch, use the facilities, and come away with a good photo.

Beyond the elephants there are other sculptures representing Trang — a colourful frog-head Tuk Tuk (one of Trang's signature icons), dugong sculptures representing the last dugong pod near Koh Libong, a Sakai forest-dweller figure, and what many people mention as the "world's smallest monument" — a tiny point you have to look carefully to find. A full circuit for photos takes about an hour. The atmosphere is an open hilltop plaza with the Banthat mountain range as a backdrop. On early monsoon mornings, sea mist sometimes drifts over the peaks in the background.

More of a roadside rest point than a ticketed attraction — there's a parking area, toilets, a tourist information centre, a royal merit pavilion, and food-and-coffee shops with mountain views on both sides of the road. Reviews from visitors consistently say it's a convenient, clean, and photo-rewarding stop. Most of the spending is just a coffee or a snack. No entry fee.

Practical note: Saturdays, Sundays, and long holidays get busy — tour vans stop here constantly, and parking may fill up in mid-morning. For cleaner shots without crowds and queues, come early or in the late afternoon near sunset. Midday sun on the hilltop is quite strong; bring a hat and water.
mustOrder: Life-size elephant sculpture herd
Frog-head Tuk Tuk — Trang's signature icon
Dugong and Sakai forest-dweller sculptures
Banthat mountain range viewpoint
blocks.bestFor: A roadside photo stop before entering Trang city
blocks.hours: Open daily (outdoor area, accessible all day)

blocks.name: Robinson Lifestyle Trang
blocks.signature: Trang's main shopping centre — Robinson, SF Cinema, food court, brand-name restaurants, children's play zone, and a section for fashion, beauty, and home goods
blocks.descHtml:
Robinson Lifestyle Trang is the main shopping centre in the city centre — the place Trang locals arrange to meet for just about everything, from a casual stroll out of the heat and rain, to shopping, watching a film, or bringing the family for a meal. As a visitor stopping through Trang who wants somewhere cool and all-in-one, this is the obvious choice: fashion, beauty, homeware, a supermarket, brand-name restaurants, a food court, a cinema, and children's activities under one roof.

The highlights people mention are the "all-in-one" quality — reviews consistently say you can find everything you need in a single pass, from food to daily items. The upper floors have SF Cinema; the ground floor has a supermarket and familiar restaurant brands from both Thai and international fast food. Families with children will find play equipment and rotating seasonal activities throughout the year. During festivals the main event space often hosts cosplay events and promotions.

The atmosphere inside is well-organized, easy to navigate, air-conditioned, and clean, with ample parking around the building. No entry fee; spending depends on what you eat and buy. A meal at the food court starts at a few hundred baht. The mall is on Phatthalung Road, Thap Thiang Sub-district, Mueang Trang District — close to the city centre, easy to reach. Open daily around 10:00–21:00.

It's popular because it's the province's largest shopping centre and both locals and tourists pass through constantly. Google reviews rate it well from a large number of visitors, who praise the cleanliness, air conditioning, and helpful staff. Small tip: evening on weekends and public holidays is busy. Coming midday or on a weekday gives you easier parking and a more relaxed browse.
mustOrder: SF Cinema on the upper floor
Food court / brand-name restaurants
Supermarket and fashion zone
Children's play area
blocks.bestFor: Beat the heat, shopping, a film, and bringing the whole family in one stop

blocks.title: Book tickets and tours in Trang in advance
blocks.text: If you want to cover multiple Trang attractions in one day without driving yourself, booking a guided tour or vehicle with driver through Klook or GetYourGuide is the easiest route. Out-of-town spots like Thung Khai botanical garden and Kantang are in separate districts, and many Trang trips can extend to Andaman islands nearby. Booking ahead also means you're not sorting logistics at the boat pier yourself.

blocks.title: What to know before visiting Trang

items.title: Having a car makes everything easier
items.text: City spots like the Clock Tower and Sra Kapang Surinthon park are walkable or Grab-accessible, but the best spots outside the city — Thung Khai, Kantang, and Khao Phap Pha — are in separate districts. Renting a car or booking a driver is the most practical option.

items.title: Carry cash for markets
items.text: Street food stalls at Cinta Garden Night Market and the railway station walking street mostly accept cash or Thai QR payments. Small bills are easier. Malls and cafés in the city accept cards.

items.title: Plan your timing around each spot
items.text: Outdoor landmarks photograph best in the morning or evening when the sun is not fierce. Evening markets open from around 17:00. The walking street in front of Trang Railway Station is lively on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays only — check the day before you plan.

items.title: Tipping is not compulsory
items.text: Restaurants and markets in Trang do not expect tips. Pay the stated price; rounding up or leaving a small amount is appreciated but not obligatory. There is no fixed tipping custom.

items.title: English menus exist in some places
items.text: Malls and cafés in the city communicate in English fairly well, but local restaurants and market stalls may only have Thai menus. A camera-translation app or pointing at photos works well; Trang locals are friendly and always ready to help.

items.title: Prepare for heat and rain
items.text: Trang is on the Andaman side and can get rain throughout the year. Carry an umbrella or light rain jacket. Bring drinking water and a hat when exploring outdoor spots like Thung Khai or Khao Phap Pha.

blocks.title: How to plan a good one-day trip in Trang
blocks.html:
With one day, base yourself in the city (Thap Thiang area) and hit the walkable city spots first. In the morning visit Trang Clock Tower and the old commercial district around it, then head to Sra Kapang Surinthon Park in the late morning when it's still shaded. Midday drive out of town to Southern Botanical Garden (Thung Khai) in Yan Ta Khao for the canopy walkway, or head south to Kantang Railway Station to photograph the old wooden building.

Come back to the city in the evening and close the trip at a night market — Cinta Garden Night Market opens around 17:00 with live music and photo zones, or if it falls on a Friday, Saturday, or Sunday, walk the street in front of Trang Railway Station and eat Trang crab noodles, Trang cake, roti, and cha chak. The Sra Kapang park evening water-curtain and dancing-fountain show is worth a second stop on the way back.

blocks.text: To explore Trang at a relaxed pace over multiple days, booking accommodation in the city centre gives you easy access to landmarks, evening markets, and local restaurants without a long commute.

faq.q: Which attractions in Trang should you not miss?
faq.a: The spots most visitors to Trang don't skip are the Trang Clock Tower — the old-town landmark in the middle of the city — Sra Kapang Surinthon Park with its dancing-fountain show in the evenings, Kantang Railway Station, a wooden building over 100 years old, and Southern Botanical Garden (Thung Khai) with its canopy walkway. Together they cover landmark fans, nature walkers, and evening market lovers.

faq.q: What are the highlights of Trang?
faq.a: The clearly verified highlights are the canopy walkway at Thung Khai — 175 metres long, up to 18 metres high, where you walk through the tree canopy and watch birds, squirrels, and monkeys — and Kantang Railway Station, the mustard-yellow hip-roof wooden building at the end of the Andaman line, registered as an ancient monument. And the dugong — the provincial symbol — represented by the Dugong Circle fountain in the middle of the city.

faq.q: Do Trang attractions charge entry fees?
faq.a: Most popular attractions on this list are free to enter — the Clock Tower, Sra Kapang Surinthon Park, Dugong Circle, Trang Andaman Gateway, Kantang Railway Station, and Southern Botanical Garden (Thung Khai). Evening markets like Cinta Garden and the railway station walking street have no entry fee — pay only for food and purchases, around 150–300 THB per person. Robinson Lifestyle Trang has no entry fee and is a mall for beating the heat and shopping.

faq.q: How do you get around and park in Trang city?
faq.a: Several city spots are in the Thap Thiang area and walkable from each other — the Clock Tower, old commercial district, and Trang Railway Station. Sra Kapang Surinthon Park, Cinta Garden Night Market, and Robinson all have parking. Out-of-town spots like Thung Khai (Yan Ta Khao District), Kantang Railway Station, and Trang Andaman Gateway (Khao Phap Pha, Na Yong District) need a private vehicle or rental car — public transport between districts is limited.

faq.q: What time do markets and evening attractions in Trang open?
faq.a: Cinta Garden Night Market opens daily around 17:00–23:00, with street food, live music, and multiple photo zones. The walking street in front of Trang Railway Station is lively Friday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings. The water-curtain and dancing-fountain show at Sra Kapang Surinthon Park is an evening show. Outdoor landmarks like the Clock Tower and Dugong Circle can be visited all day, though evenings give the best light and photos.
